TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Economic Development Commission 
Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
5:30 PM, November 10, 2026 
 
 
 
Hamden Government 
Center 
2750 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
Tel:  (203) 287-7070 
Fax:  (203) 287-7075 
 Click to View Agenda   
  
1. CALL TO ORDER 
  
 The meeting was called to order by Chair Commissioner K. Good at 5:32 PM. 
2. ATTENDANCE 
  
 The roll was called by the Clerk, and the following members were present: 
 
Present 
Commissioner Ken Good, Chair 
Commissioner Petra Gardella 
Commissioner Tammy Robinson 
Commissioner Anthony J. DelGrego 
Commissioner Maggie Murolo 
Commissioner Romeo Ibanez 
 
Absent 
Commissioner Howard K. Hill 
 
Also in attendance were Steve Fontana, Economic Development Director, who attended in 
person; Briana J. Belton-Robinson, Boards and Commissions Clerk; and three members of 
the public, who attended virtually. 
 
Roll Call Summary: Present, Voting: 6; Present, Not Voting: 0; Absent: 1; Excused: 0. 
3. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES 
  
 
 
  1. Meeting Minutes for October 13, 2026  
  Chairman K. Good requested a motion to adopt the minutes from Tuesday, November 
10th, 2026: 
 
Commissioner T. Robinson moved to approve the minutes, and Commissioner M. 
Maggie seconded the motion.
Yes 
Commissioner K. Good, Chair 
Commissioner T. Robinson 
Commissioner A.J. DelGrego 
Commissioner M. Murolo 
Commissioner R. Ibanez 
Commissioner P. Gardella 
 
No 
 
Absent 
Commissioner H.K. Hill 
 
The motion passed. 
• Roll Call Vote Summary: Yes 6, No 0, Abstentions 0, Absent 1 
  
4. PUBLIC COMMENT 
  
 Sarah Clark addressed the Commission and requested updates regarding the High 
Meadows development project and the former Spring Glen Hardware property. 
 
Ms. Clark also expressed appreciation for the Commission's return to in-person meetings 
and requested that future meeting notices clearly identify opportunities for members of the 
public to attend in person, as the published agenda identified only Zoom participation. 
 
Chairman K. Good thanked Ms. Clark for her comments. 
5. CORRESPONDENCE 
There will be a brief summary of the correspondence submitted between the last 
correspondence update and this one. This includes but is not limited to any 
correspondence with council members that members wish to submit for the record. It can 
also include written communication to the council from the administration, community 
members, etc.   
 The Boards and Commissions Clerk confirmed that no additional correspondence had 
been received since the previous meeting. 
6. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)  
 No executive session was held. 
7. CHAIRMAN'S REPORTS 
  
 
 
  1. Business Community Update  
  Chairman K. Good reported 63 recent business registrations in Hamden, representing 
industries including professional and technology services, healthcare, behavioral 
services, construction, skilled trades, real estate, property management, retail, food
services, and personal services. 
 
Several registrations were concentrated along Dixwell Avenue, Whitney Avenue, Mix 
Avenue, and State Street. Chairman K. Good identified five registrations at 235 
Dixwell Avenue and three at 1840 State Street, noting that further review may be 
warranted to distinguish actively operating businesses from entities using shared 
business addresses. 
 
Chairman K. Good highlighted the following business and development activities: 
 
Cultivate Behavioral Science and Education: The company opened an applied 
behavior analysis therapy clinic at 105 Sanford Street on October 19, 2026. The 
location represents the company's second Hamden facility, seventh Connecticut 
facility, and 50th nationwide. 
 
Eli Center of Contemporary Art: The organization is seeking to establish a 
permanent location in Hamden and has submitted applications for special permit and 
site plan approval for an art gallery and exhibition space at 131 Leeder Hill Drive, Unit 
7. Chairman K. Good expressed support for expanding the Town's cultural and artistic 
business community. 
 
Fire Station No. 2: Chairman K. Good reported progress regarding the proposed 
replacement fire station at 466 Putnam Avenue. The Town is pursuing additional 
funding through the State's Small Town Economic Assistance and Community 
Investment funding opportunities, including the Community Investment Fund's tenth 
funding round, to support the project. Further discussion was deferred to the Director's 
Report. 
  2. EDC Alliances  
  Commissioner R. Ibanez provided an update regarding ongoing efforts to establish 
partnerships between the Town of Hamden, local businesses, and Quinnipiac 
University through its developing Solution Center initiative. 
 
Commissioner R. Ibanez explained that the initiative is designed to connect local 
businesses, nonprofit organizations, and municipal departments with university 
students and faculty to address organizational challenges while providing students 
with practical, experiential learning opportunities. 
 
The proposed partnership would offer participating organizations access to university 
resources in areas such as business consulting, cybersecurity, technology, 
operational improvement, and workforce development. 
 
Commissioner R. Ibanez highlighted Quinnipiac University's student-led Cybersecurity 
Program as a potential resource for local businesses and organizations seeking 
assistance with cybersecurity-related challenges. He emphasized the importance of 
making these opportunities accessible to Hamden's business community. 
 
Commissioner R. Ibanez also discussed the differences between the proposed 
Quinnipiac University partnership and ongoing discussions with the University of New 
Haven. While the University of New Haven's approach would emphasize faculty-led
assistance supported by students, Quinnipiac University's model would focus primarily 
on student-led experiential learning. 
 
The Commission discussed opportunities to strengthen relationships with local higher 
education institutions, support small-business development, and improve workforce 
readiness and talent retention. 
 
Commissioner R. Ibanez identified Brooke Penders, Director of Employer Relations, 
Career and Experiential Learning at Quinnipiac University, as a primary university 
contact for organizations interested in exploring partnership opportunities. 
 
University Contact: 
Brooke Penders 
Director of Employer Relations, Career and Experiential Learning 
Quinnipiac University 
Email: Brooke.Penders@quinnipiac.edu 
 
Commissioner R. Ibanez moved to include the informational flyer for Quinnipiac 
University's student-led Cybersecurity Program for organizations in the agenda packet 
accompanying the November 10, 2026, Economic Development Commission meeting 
minutes. 
 
Yes

Commissioner T. Robinson

Commissioner P. Gardella 
 
No 
 
Absent

• Roll Call Vote Summary: Yes 6, No 0, Abstentions 0, Absent 1 
 
  3. Town Center Master Plan  
  Chairman K. Good and Director S. Fontana provided updates following the third 
advisory committee meeting for the Town Center Master Plan. 
 
Chairman K. Good explained that the planning team is evaluating individual properties 
based on building conditions, development potential, opportunities for parcel 
consolidation, disconnected land uses, and the potential to stimulate additional 
economic activity. 
 
The planning process focuses on underutilized properties, aging buildings, excessive 
parking areas, and opportunities to improve pedestrian connectivity.
Chairman K. Good clarified that properties identified as potential redevelopment 
opportunities would not be required to redevelop. Rather, the recommendations are 
intended to encourage voluntary reinvestment and illustrate possible future uses. 
 
Director S. Fontana reported that the planning team had received more than 400 
survey responses, exceeding its initial goal of 250 participants. However, most 
responses came from individuals over age 50. The planning team is seeking greater 
participation from younger residents to ensure that the recommendations reflect a 
broader demographic. 
 
The planning team intends to present two alternative development concepts 
addressing residential, commercial, entertainment, and mixed-use opportunities 
throughout the Town Center. 
 
The planning team announced a public design workshop for Wednesday, November 
18, 2026, at Miller Memorial Library. The workshop is scheduled from 5:30 pm to 6:30 
pm, followed by an open house from 6:30 pm to 7:00 pm. 
 
Chairman K. Good encouraged commissioners and residents to attend and provide 
feedback on the proposed concepts. 
 
Director S. Fontana stated that the Town Center Master Plan is expected to be 
completed around January 2027. 
8. DIRECTOR'S REPORT 
  
 Former Hamden Middle School, 560 Newhall Street 
 
Director S. Fontana provided an update on demolishing the remaining former Hamden 
Middle School building at 560 Newhall Street. He reported that demolition had been 
delayed because the process requires substantial amounts of water to control airborne dust 
and debris. However, using water presents challenges during colder winter months. The 
Town intends to use the intervening months to complete preparatory work and expects to 
begin demolition in earnest around March 2027, weather permitting. 
 
Director S. Fontana stated that after demolition, the Mayor's Office intends to begin a 
community engagement process in spring 2027 to gather residents' input on potential 
future uses of the property. 
 
Chairman K. Good asked whether the property was classified as a brownfield site. 
 
Director S. Fontana described the property as a remediated brownfield containing residual 
soil contamination. He explained that the site had been capped with approximately four feet 
of clean fill in certain areas, with pavement and existing foundations also serving as 
protective barriers. The property is subject to an Environmental Land Use Restriction 
(ELUR), which establishes conditions for future development and protects against 
exposure to remaining contamination. 
Director S. Fontana explained that future construction would be possible, including 
development requiring new foundations, provided that the proposed plans appropriately
address the ELUR and any contaminated soil disturbed during excavation. 
 
Commissioners discussed potential residential, commercial, industrial, mixed-use, and 
urban agricultural opportunities. Director Fontana emphasized that future uses would 
require consideration of environmental conditions, development costs, and neighborhood 
preferences. 
 
No specific redevelopment proposal was endorsed. 
 
High Meadows Redevelopment Project: The Community Builders 
 
Director S. Fontana provided an update on the High Meadows redevelopment project, for 
which the Town selected The Community Builders (TCB) as the preferred developer 
through its request-for-proposals process. The proposal involves redeveloping the former 
state-owned property into affordable housing, including rental housing, senior housing, and 
a smaller homeownership component. Director S. Fontana reported that TCB continues to 
develop its financing and implementation plans. The project requires coordination among 
multiple public funding sources, each with separate eligibility requirements, approval 
processes, and timelines. Existing state legislation sets a transaction deadline of June 30, 
2027, with a possible extension to December 31, 2027. Director Fontana stated that the 
project would likely require an additional legislative extension, as the anticipated closing 
date is approximately summer 2028. 
 
He reported that the Town's legislative delegation had expressed support for extending the 
deadline if necessary. 
 
Development Financing and Alternative Developers 
 
Commissioner R. Ibanez expressed concern regarding rising interest rates and the 
possibility that unfavorable financial conditions could affect TCB's ability to complete the 
project. He asked whether other developers or organizations might be interested in the 
property if TCB could not proceed. 
 
Director S. Fontana explained that interest rates were not currently the primary concern 
because the project would rely substantially on public subsidies, affordable housing tax 
credits, and other preferential financing mechanisms. He also noted that potential 
reductions in tariffs on Canadian construction materials could improve construction costs. 
Director S. Fontana clarified that if TCB withdrew from the project, the Town would need to 
issue a new request for proposals, as no other applicant had submitted a complete and 
satisfactory proposal during the previous selection process. He emphasized that TCB 
remained committed to the development and that the Town would continue supporting its 
efforts. 
 
Commissioner R. Ibanez also asked about the project's underwriting and whether financing 
would primarily come from federal, state, private, or conventional lending sources. 
 
Director S. Fontana explained that the project would likely rely heavily on subsidized 
financing, including affordable housing tax credits and public funding, rather than 
conventional private-market financing alone. The developer would present the final 
financing structure as the project advances.
Traffic, Access, and Site Development 
 
Chairman K. Good raised concerns regarding increased traffic and potential access to 
State Street. 
 
Director S. Fontana explained that the site's configuration, wetlands, and stormwater 
conditions could complicate the construction of an additional vehicular entrance. The Town 
has discussed opportunities for pedestrian access to State Street to improve connectivity 
with public transportation. 
 
Commissioner R. Ibanez suggested exploring whether nearby property owners could 
provide easements or opportunities for additional access. 
 
Director S. Fontana stated that the developer would be expected to complete a traffic study 
as part of the planning and land-use approval process. 
 
Commissioners also discussed the property's existing buildings. Director S. Fontana noted 
that the buildings may contain asbestos or other hazardous materials and are generally 
unsuitable for conversion into the proposed multifamily housing development. 
 
Property Taxes and Municipal Revenue 
 
Chairman K. Good asked whether the property would generate municipal tax revenue, 
given the State of Connecticut's current ownership. 
 
Director S. Fontana explained that the property currently contributes to the Town's revenue 
through the State's payment-in-lieu-of-taxes program, which uses a prescribed 
reimbursement structure for eligible state-owned properties. Following transfer to private 
ownership and redevelopment, the property would leave the state-owned property 
reimbursement system and become subject to municipal property taxation. Director S. 
Fontana stated that the difference, or delta, between the existing state reimbursement and 
the potential future tax revenue could produce a long-term financial benefit for Hamden. He 
also noted that the development could generate building permit fees and other municipal 
revenues during construction. 
 
No formal financial analysis or tax incentive proposal was presented. 
 
Former Spring Glen Hardware, 1666 Whitney Avenue 
 
Director S. Fontana provided an update on the former Spring Glen Hardware property at 
1666 Whitney Avenue, which has remained vacant since early 2023. 
He reported that the Town's Building Official had worked with the property owners to 
address site safety concerns. The previously excavated area had been filled to comply with 
applicable requirements, and the property remained fenced. Director S. Fontana and Town 
Planner Eugene Livshits recently met with the property owners to discuss potential 
redevelopment concepts. The owners are consolidating feedback and preparing a revised 
development proposal for public consideration. Preliminary concepts include two small 
retail spaces, one facing Whitney Avenue and another facing Russell Street.
Chairman K. Good asked whether the property could accommodate another hardware 
store, emphasizing the value of neighborhood businesses and the convenience Spring 
Glen Hardware previously provided. 
 
Director S. Fontana stated that a hardware business could potentially occupy one of the 
proposed retail spaces if a suitable operator expressed interest. 
 
The Commission discussed the importance of ensuring that any new development 
complements the surrounding neighborhood and avoids excessive building density. 
 
Director Fontana anticipated receiving revised plans within the following one to two months. 
 
Mount Carmel Sewer Extension Study 
 
Director S. Fontana reported that the Mount Carmel sewer extension study determined that 
extending sewer infrastructure along the Whitney Avenue corridor toward the Cheshire 
town line is technically feasible. However, the project would require substantial financial 
investment. The study has been divided into three potential phases. Director Fontana 
explained that the first phase would be the most expensive because it would require 
installing foundational infrastructure needed to support subsequent phases. The Town 
intends to pursue planning and design funding through the South Central Regional Council 
of Governments (SCRCOG). Director S. Fontana stated that the Town would also seek 
support from state and federal representatives to advance the project, emphasizing its 
potential to support commercial development, environmental improvements, and economic 
growth along the Whitney Avenue corridor. 
 
Commissioners discussed Quinnipiac University's proximity to the proposed infrastructure 
improvements. 
 
Director Fontana said the university had been informed of the project and expressed 
support for the broader economic development opportunities the extension could create. 
 
Community Investment Fund: Round 10 Applications 
 
Director S. Fontana reported that the Town is preparing applications for the tenth round of 
the State's Community Investment Fund (CIF) program, with applications due in early 
December 2026. The Town intends to submit one implementation grant application and 
one planning grant application. 
 
Fire Station No. 2 at 466 Putnam Avenue 
 
The implementation grant would seek the remaining funding necessary to complete the 
replacement of Fire Station No. 2 at 466 Putnam Avenue, near Putnam Avenue and 
Gallagher Road. Director S. Fontana estimated that approximately 75% to 80% of the 
project is currently funded. He said the remaining funding gap may be about $4 million, 
although Stephen White would need to confirm the final amount. The Town hopes to 
secure the remaining funding without substantially reducing the project's planned scope. 
 
Dixwell Avenue Corridor Revitalization Master Plan
The proposed planning grant would support a comprehensive revitalization study of Dixwell 
Avenue, extending from the Route 15/Connelly Parkway area south to the New Haven 
town line. The proposed study would examine infrastructure, streetscape improvements, 
zoning, redevelopment opportunities, transportation connectivity, and the suitability of 
specific properties for future development. Properties of interest include the existing Fire 
Station No. 2 site at 71 Circular Avenue and the former Kramer Iron property at 400 North 
Street. Director S. Fontana reported that the City of New Haven is interested in pursuing a 
parallel revitalization planning initiative along its portion of Dixwell Avenue, extending from 
the New Haven Green north to the Hamden town line. The two municipalities hope to 
coordinate their efforts to establish a cohesive redevelopment vision for the entire corridor. 
 
Director S. Fontana estimated that Hamden's planning grant request would be 
approximately $250,000. The proposed planning initiative would also complement 
anticipated bus rapid transit improvements and other investments in southern Hamden. 
 
Commissioners discussed the relationship between the proposed corridor plan, the former 
Hamden Middle School redevelopment, and the ongoing environmental remediation of the 
Six Lakes property. 
 
Director Fontana emphasized the importance of coordinating these initiatives to support 
long-term revitalization throughout southern Hamden. 
 
Additional Commercial Development Updates 
Hamden Plaza, Panda Express 
 
Director S. Fontana reported that Panda Express plans to open in the former Panera Bread 
space at Hamden Plaza in early 2027. The property owner intends to subdivide the existing 
space into two commercial units. Director Fontana is working with the property owner to 
identify another suitable restaurant or fast-casual business for the adjoining space. 
 
Old Coach Highway Development 
 
Director S. Fontana announced that the Planning and Zoning Commission would hold a 
public hearing on November 24, 2026, regarding a proposed development on Old Coach 
Highway. 
 
The developer is expected to present the proposal and respond to questions from residents 
and commissioners. 
 
Eli Center of Contemporary Art 
 
Director S. Fontana reiterated the Town's interest in welcoming the Eli Center of 
Contemporary Art to Hamden. The organization is pursuing a location on Leeder Hill Drive, 
and Director Fontana expressed optimism that the center could open within the next 
several months. 
 
He emphasized the importance of attracting cultural organizations and strengthening 
Hamden's identity as a destination for artistic and creative activities. 
 
Southern Connecticut State University and Urban League Entrepreneurship
Programs 
 
Director Fontana reported attending a graduation ceremony at Southern Connecticut State 
University for participants in the Urban League of Southern Connecticut's DNA of an 
Entrepreneur program. The program helps aspiring entrepreneurs develop business ideas 
and understand the fundamentals of starting and operating a business. 
 
Director Fontana reported that as many as five Hamden residents participated in the most 
recent cohort. He also highlighted the Urban League's business accelerator program, 
which supports established businesses seeking to expand operations and increase 
revenue. 
 
Director Fontana encouraged commissioners to refer interested Hamden entrepreneurs to 
the Economic Development Department for assistance connecting with these programs. 
 
Hamden Chamber of Commerce Choice Awards 
Director Fontana announced that the Hamden Chamber of Commerce Choice Awards 
Dinner would take place on Thursday, November 12, 2026, at 6:00 PM at Cascade. 
 
He invited interested commissioners to attend and asked those wishing to participate to 
notify his office of their availability and dinner selections. 
 
Additional Questions and Discussion 
Chairman K. Good requested updates regarding Paier College, the former Stop & Shop 
location on Putnam Avenue, and the Town's clock tower. 
 
Director S. Fontana reported that there were no significant updates regarding Paier 
College. Regarding the former Stop & Shop property, he stated that he continued 
contacting potential grocery operators but had not received any commitments or 
substantive developments. Director S. Fontana also reported that Stephen White and his 
staff continued reviewing matters associated with the clock tower, although no additional 
information was available. 
 
Commissioner R. Ibanez suggested that the Town consider developing a centralized online 
resource to help local businesses identify available entrepreneurship programs, technical 
assistance, and other economic development services. 
 
Director S. Fontana supported the idea and suggested that a future summer intern could 
help prepare a business resource guide. 
 
Commissioner R. Ibanez also commended the Town's recent improvements in 
communicating municipal meetings, programs, and community opportunities through social 
media. 
 
Director S. Fontana acknowledged the efforts of a staff member, Crystal, who assists with 
the Town's public communications. 
9. OLD BUSINESS 
  
 No old business was presented.
10. NEW BUSINESS 
  
 No new business was presented. 
11. ADJOURNMENT 
  
 Commissioner P. Gardella moved to adjourn; Commissioner R. Ibanez seconded.  
 
The motion passed unanimously. 
 
The meeting adjourned at 6:55 PM.
